qs.q: What is the gold diagnostic tool for confirming Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) in patients with systemic sclerosis?
qs.e: Right-sided heart catheterization is the gold diagnostic tool to confirm pulmonary arterial hypertension, whereas echocardiography is used as the initial investigation. PFTs may show an isolated low DLCO, but catheterization is definitive.

qs.q: Which autoantibody is noted to be extremely specific for CREST syndrome and is associated with the limited subset of systemic sclerosis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and digital ulcers?
qs.e: Anti-centromere antibodies are extremely specific for CREST syndrome and are linked to the limited subset of systemic sclerosis and pulmonary arterial hypertension. In contrast, Scl-70 is associated with the diffuse subset and ILD.

qs.q: What is the gold standard diagnostic tool for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in systemic sclerosis?
qs.e: The note identifies right-sided heart catheterization as the gold diagnostic tool for PAH. Echocardiography is the first investigation to order but is not the gold standard.
